q-97161.name: Question 1
q-97161.problem: Given that $X∼\text{Geom}(0.1),$ compute $P(4<X\le 10)$ rounded to $4$ decimal places.
q-97161.worked_solution:
If $X∼\text{Geom}(p),$ then $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}(1-p)^{x-1}p, & x=1,2,3,… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Here, $X∼\text{Geom}(0.1),$ so the distribution of $X$ in this case is

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{(0.9)}^{x-1}(0.1), & x=1,2,3,… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(4<X\le 10) & =P(X\in \{5,6,7,8,9,10\}) \\  & =P(X=5)+P(X=6)+P(X=7)+ \\  & \,P(X=8)+P(X=9)+P(X=10) \\  & =f(5)+f(6)+f(7)+f(8)+f(9)+f(10) \\  & ={(0.9)}^{4}(0.1)+{(0.9)}^{5}(0.1)+{(0.9)}^{6}(0.1)+ \\  & \,{(0.9)}^{7}(0.1)+{(0.9)}^{8}(0.1)+{(0.9)}^{9}(0.1) \\  & ≈0.3074.\end{aligned}
$$

q-97183.name: Question 2
q-97183.problem: Given $X∼\text{Geom}(\frac{5}{8}),$ compute $P(X\ge 3)$ rounded to $4$ decimal places.
q-97183.worked_solution:
If $X∼\text{Geom}(p),$ then $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}(1-p)^{x-1}p, & x=1,2,3,… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Here, $X∼\text{Geom}(\frac{5}{8}),$ so the distribution of $X$ in this case is

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{(\frac{3}{8})}^{x-1}(\frac{5}{8}), & x=1,2,3… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

There are infinitely many values of $X$ such that $X\ge 3.$ However, we can simplify the computation by using the complement instead:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 3) & =1-P(X<3)\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the complement, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<3) & =P(X\in \{1,2\}) \\  & =P(X=1)+P(X=2) \\  & =f(1)+f(2) \\  & ={(\frac{3}{8})}^{0}(\frac{5}{8})+{(\frac{3}{8})}^{1}(\frac{5}{8}) \\  & ≈0.8594.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 3) & =1-P(X<3) \\  & ≈1-0.8594 \\  & =0.1406.\end{aligned}
$$

q-335528.worked_solution:
If $X∼\text{Geom}(p),$ then $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}(1-p)^{x-1}p, & x=1,2,3,… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Here, $X∼\text{Geom}(0.7),$ so the distribution of $X$ in this case is

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}(0.3)^{x-1}(0.7), & x=1,2,3,… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

There are infinitely many values of $X$ such that $X>5.$ However, we can simplify the computation by using the complement instead:

$$
P(X>5)=1-P(X\le 5)
$$

Computing the complement, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 5) & =P(X\in \{1,2,3,4,5\}) \\  & =P(X=1)+P(X=2)+P(X=3)+P(X=4)+P(X=5) \\  & =f(1)+f(2)+f(3)+f(4)+f(5) \\  & =(0.3)^{0}(0.7)+(0.3)^{1}(0.7)+(0.3)^{2}(0.7)+(0.3)^{3}(0.7)+(0.3)^{4}(0.7) \\  & =0.99757.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>5) & =1-P(X\le 5) \\  & =1-0.99757 \\  & ≈0.0024.\end{aligned}
